metaDescription: Six heavy-duty garden carts rated from 600 to 1000 lb, compared on poly versus steel beds, expandable sides, tire design and how each handles big loads.
introParagraphs: The upper end of our garden cart range is where capacity numbers climb past half a ton. This lineup includes carts rated at 880, 900 and 1000 lb alongside the 600 lb Gorilla Carts dump cart, so the real question is less how much each carries and more how each one behaves when it is full. We evaluated all six on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at bed material, tires, handles and unloading.

Heavy-rated carts are not automatically better for ordinary yards. A 1000 lb steel wagon is overkill for potting soil and can be awkward to turn, while a poly dump cart with expandable sides can move a surprising amount of mulch in fewer trips. The best pick depends on whether you haul bulk material, bulky objects or both.

Below we explain what this tier buys, where the compromises are, and which cart suits which job. A rating is a limit, not a target, so keep loads centered over the axle and check tires and fasteners before every big haul.

products.name: Sekey Steel Garden Cart, 1000 lb, Removable Sides
products.description:
The Sekey carries the highest rating in the group at 1000 lb, and it pairs that number with practical features. Mesh sides come off to turn the box into a flatbed, so bulky items like planters, lumber and rolls of sod do not need to fit inside a bucket. The 10 inch rubber tires cushion the ride over lawns and gravel.

A handle that rotates through 180 degrees helps with steering and with stowing the cart upright. The maker describes the frame as reinforced to avoid the bending that flimsy carts suffer, which matters at a four-figure rating. Two-in-one use makes it a general yard workhorse.

Steel means weight and eventual rust if the finish chips, and a loaded 1000 lb cart is hard to hold back on a slope. Check the exact model, tire type and included parts on the listing, since details can vary. Compared with the BILT HARD 900 lb poly cart, it does not dump. Compared with the VEVOR, it adds a rotating handle and a higher rating. For a yard with a lot of bulky hauling, it is the best-rounded wagon.
products.bestFor: Large yards that haul bulky items as well as bagged material.
pros: Highest rating in the group at 1000 lb
Mesh sides come off for flatbed hauling
Handle rotates 180 degrees for steering
Rubber tires soften lawn and gravel runs
cons: Heavy to hold back on slopes when full
Steel finish needs protecting from rust
Model details should be checked on the page

products.name: BILT HARD 900 lb Poly Garden Dump Cart, 5 Cu Ft
products.description:
This BILT HARD dump cart has the biggest standard bed here at 5 cubic feet, and it can grow. Side expansion slots accept boards you supply, which lets you stretch the volume when hauling bulky leaves or straw. The bed is heavy-duty poly on a steel frame, and the cart is rated for up to 900 lb.

Ten inch pneumatic tires give traction over grass, dirt and gravel, and a quick-release system tips the bed to empty it. That combination suits owners who spread mulch in spring and rake leaves in autumn, and who would otherwise be shovelling out of a box.

Extra volume does not raise the weight limit, so a tall stack of light material is fine while a full bed of wet soil can approach the rating quickly. Pneumatic tires also need a pump now and then. Compared with the CAMMOO 900 lb, it offers air-filled tires instead of no-flat ones, and a larger bed. Compared with the Gorilla Carts 600 lb, it adds capacity and expansion. It is a smart choice for seasonal bulk work and a good value for the volume.
products.bestFor: Seasonal bulk jobs like mulch, leaves and straw.
pros: Largest standard bed at 5 cubic feet
Side slots allow home-made expansion
Quick-release tips the bed to unload
Rated up to 900 lb on a steel frame
cons: Added boards do not raise weight limit
Air-filled tires need an occasional pump
Poly bed lacks a removable flatbed mode

products.name: BILT HARD 880 lb Flat-Free Garden Cart, Removable Sides
products.description:
At 880 lb this steel garden wagon offers more than double the rating of the entry 400 lb BILT HARD cart. All four wheels are 10 inch no-flat tires, which eliminate the chore of checking pressure. Removable sides let you switch between a box and a flat platform, and a handle that rotates 180 degrees helps with steering.

The maker highlights straightforward assembly, and the listing says you can put it together with clear instructions. That matters for a cart this size, because awkward assembly is a common complaint with steel wagons. Durable construction is advertised for heavy loads and rough outdoor use.

Solid tires can feel harsher than pneumatic ones on rough ground, and a four-wheel layout turns wider than a two-wheel barrow. It does not dump, so unloading is by hand or shovel. Compared with the Sekey, it has a lower rating and a smaller feature list but a simpler tire arrangement. Compared with the BILT HARD poly model, it swaps tipping for a flatbed mode. A sensible pick for owners who want a tough wagon without tire maintenance.
products.bestFor: Heavy hauling with no tire maintenance and easy assembly.
pros: No-flat tires on all four wheels
Removable sides give a flat platform
Rotating handle eases steering and storage
Listing highlights straightforward assembly
cons: Solid tires can ride harshly on rough ground
No dumping action for bulk loads
Wider turns than a two-wheel barrow

products.name: CAMMOO 900 lb No-Flat Garden Dump Cart
products.description:
CAMMOO takes the no-flat approach to a 900 lb dump cart. Ten inch tires run without air, backed by dual steel bearings, and expandable side slots accept boards to lift capacity in volume. A thickened steel frame with diagonal rods on the rear supports forms a stable triangle.

This is the cart for owners tired of fixing flats. Solid tires never leak, and the dump design lets the bed tip so heavy material slides out. At this rating the tire and bearing design matters, because a cart that is rarely used often fails by a flat or seized wheel.

Be careful with the listing: the brand also sells a 600 lb version, so confirm you are ordering the 900 lb one. The brand is newer, so treat its record as an early signal. Compared with the BILT HARD poly dump cart, it uses solid tires rather than pneumatic, which feels firmer on rough ground. Compared with the Sekey, it dumps but does not convert into a flatbed. For people who want a cart that sits ready in the garage, it is a pleasing balance of capacity and low upkeep.
products.bestFor: Infrequent heavy haulers who dislike flat-tire surprises.
pros: No-flat tires remove the pump routine
Dual steel bearings keep wheels turning
Side slots add volume with your own boards
Triangle bracing on the rear supports
cons: Easy to confuse with the brand's 600 lb model
Newer brand with a shorter record

products.name: VEVOR Heavy Duty Steel Garden Cart, 900 lb Wagon
products.description:
VEVOR builds its wagon from high-strength Q235 steel and adds three support beams beneath the base. The cart converts between a fenced box and a flatbed, so it can haul loose material one day and long boards the next. It is rated at 900 lb and rides on 10 inch wheels.

The design emphasizes strength and flexibility rather than dumping. Four wheels spread the load and keep the platform level, which helps with fragile pots and heavy stone alike. For a mixed-use yard, that versatility is its strongest argument.

The listing should be checked for the current tire type and assembly details before ordering. It lacks a rotating handle, so steering is simpler than on the Sekey and BILT HARD wagons. The brand is not as established as Gorilla Carts. Compared with the Sekey, it offers 100 lb less rating but the same wagon-style flexibility. Compared with the CAMMOO 900 lb, it cannot dump but converts to a flatbed. Choose it if you want a solid steel base with two working modes and you are comfortable maintaining the finish.
products.bestFor: Mixed-use yards that alternate between loose and long loads.
pros: Converts between fenced box and flatbed
Three base beams support heavy loads
Q235 steel body built for 900 lb
Four-wheel platform stays level
cons: No rotating handle for easy steering
Tire type and assembly need checking
Does not tip to dump bulk material

products.name: Gorilla Carts 600 lb Poly Garden Dump Cart, 4 Cu Ft
products.description:
Gorilla Carts brings the most recognisable dump cart design to a lineup of heavier-rated rivals. Its poly bed holds 4 cubic feet with a 600 lb rating, and a patented quick-release system tips the load out safely with little effort. Tight-turning steering and four-wheel balance keep loads controlled on uneven ground.

Owners often choose it for familiarity: a design that has been copied by many competitors, with 10 inch pneumatic tires that ride smoothly. The listing positions it for soil, gravel, compost, plants and mulch, which covers the majority of garden hauling.

It carries less than any other cart in this group, and pneumatic tires bring the usual pump-and-patch duty. If your loads regularly approach half a ton, look at the 900 lb carts instead. Compared with the BILT HARD poly cart, it has a smaller bed and no side expansion. Compared with the Sekey, it is a pure dump cart and cannot become a flatbed. Its appeal lies in handling and a proven shape, not in headline capacity, which is why it holds a place even among stronger-rated rivals.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want a proven dump design and tight steering.
pros: Patented quick release tips loads safely
Tight-turning steering on uneven ground
Smooth ride from pneumatic tires
Poly bed will not rust like steel
cons: Lowest weight rating in this group
No side expansion slots for volume

buyingCriteria.explanation: Weight and volume are separate limits. The BILT HARD poly cart offers 5 cubic feet at 900 lb, the BILT HARD 880 lb wagon and Gorilla Carts both use 4 cubic feet, and the Sekey is rated at 1000 lb. A cubic foot of wet soil can weigh well over 70 lb, so a full 4 cubic foot bed can approach the limit faster than you expect.

Material changes how the cart ages. The Gorilla Carts and BILT HARD 900 lb dump cart use poly beds that resist rust and hose clean, while the Sekey, VEVOR and BILT HARD 880 lb use steel. Steel takes impacts better but needs touch-ups. Pick poly for wet climates and steel for rough abuse.

Solid tires cost you ride comfort and save you maintenance. The CAMMOO and BILT HARD 880 lb carts use no-flat tires, the Gorilla Carts and BILT HARD poly cart use pneumatic ones, and the Sekey uses rubber. If your cart sits for months, choose solid tires. If it travels long distances over soft ground, air gives a smoother roll.

These two features rarely come together. The BILT HARD poly cart, CAMMOO and Gorilla Carts tip to unload, while the Sekey, VEVOR and BILT HARD 880 lb convert to flatbeds. Bulk material favors dumping. Bulky objects favor a flat deck. Decide which job you do more often.

At high ratings, steering matters because a loaded cart is heavy. The Sekey and BILT HARD 880 lb include handles that rotate 180 degrees, while the VEVOR has a simpler layout. The Gorilla Carts is known for tight-turning steering. Try to picture your gate and path width before choosing.

Some listings in this class are easy to misread. CAMMOO sells both 600 and 900 lb versions, and the Sekey and VEVOR listings should be checked for current tire type and included parts. Confirm the rating, tire and accessories on the product page right before you buy.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and frame
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared ratings and construction. The Sekey leads at 1000 lb, the VEVOR, CAMMOO and BILT HARD poly cart sit at 900 lb, the BILT HARD wagon at 880 lb, and the Gorilla Carts at 600 lb. Bracing details such as the CAMMOO triangle and VEVOR beams added credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Tires and wheels
howWeEvaluated.description: Tire type and size were reviewed. Two carts use no-flat tires, two use pneumatic, and the Sekey uses rubber. Maintenance burden and ride comfort were weighed against each other.

howWeEvaluated.title: Unloading and bed design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each cart empties and adapts. The BILT HARD poly cart and Gorilla Carts dump, the Sekey and VEVOR convert to flatbeds, and the BILT HARD 880 lb has removable sides. Expandable slots on two carts earned extra credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We examined handles and turning. Rotating handles on the Sekey and BILT HARD 880 lb help steering, and the Gorilla Carts promotes tight turns. Heavy carts that stay manageable scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and verification
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged what each cart delivers for a modest spend and how clearly the listing describes it. Mix-ups like the CAMMOO's two ratings were flagged. Thin or inconsistent listings lost points.

faq.q: Do I need a 900 lb cart at home?
faq.a: Usually not. Most households move under 400 lb at a time, so a 600 lb Gorilla Carts or CAMMOO is enough. The 880 to 1000 lb carts suit heavy stone, wet soil and large properties.

faq.q: Which is better, the Sekey or the VEVOR?
faq.a: The Sekey is rated at 1000 lb and adds a handle that rotates 180 degrees plus removable mesh sides. The VEVOR is rated at 900 lb with fenced and flatbed modes. Choose the Sekey for higher rating and steering, the VEVOR for a simpler steel base.

faq.q: Do bed expansion slots raise capacity?
faq.a: They raise volume, not the weight limit. The BILT HARD poly cart and CAMMOO 900 lb both have slots. Use them for light bulky loads such as leaves and straw.
They suit carts that sit unused or work on thorny ground, as on the CAMMOO and BILT HARD 880 lb. The tradeoff is a firmer ride. If you move a lot over rough terrain, pneumatic tires may feel better.

faq.q: How do I confirm the right model?
faq.a: Read the listing title for the rating, check the tire type and the accessories list. CAMMOO sells both 600 and 900 lb versions, so confirm which one you are ordering.

faq.q: How should I maintain a steel cart?
faq.a: Wipe it dry after rain, touch up chips with outdoor paint and store it under cover. Check bolts and wheel bearings each season. Poly beds need only a rinse.

Typically larger bearings, more established warranties and powered or tow-behind carts. For a home garden, the picks here already cover the realistic range. Spend more only for commercial-scale hauling.
